#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --job-name=auto_encoder_type1
#   --partition=Hercules
#   --nodes=1
#   --ntasks-per-node=4
#   --mem-per-cpu=16G
#   --gres=gpu:TitanV:1
#   --time=24:00:00

#flux: --job-name=auto_encoder_type1
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 4
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=24h

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem-per-cpu=16G
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres=gpu:TitanV:1
# Flux GPU requests/type constraints are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU (or without a TitanV), causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm option: --partition=Hercules
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run on different hardware or with different limits/priority (or be rejected by policy).

# Omitted Slurm option: --ntasks-per-node=4 (explicit per-node placement)
# Flux does not have a universally portable batch directive for tasks-per-node.
# Performance implication: if the job were to span multiple nodes, rank placement might differ; here we force -N 1 to preserve intent.

module load pytorch/1.6.0-anaconda3-cuda10.2

pip install --no-index --upgrade pip

conda install -c akode atari-py

# If this program is single-process, requesting -n 4 may waste resources.
# Preserve the Slurm request by launching under Flux.
flux run -n 4 -c 1 python Type_1.py

reasons: The original Slurm job required 1 TitanV GPU (`--gres=gpu:TitanV:1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.

The original Slurm job requested memory per CPU (`--mem-per-cpu=16G`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job and risk OOM.

The original Slurm job specified a partition (`--partition=Hercules`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/partition selection; on sites where this affects eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.
